title: Buffer Small File Writes
subtitle: Batch small records in memory to amortize stream flush and system-call overhead.

metrics.label: CPU cycles
metrics.explanation: Cycles include formatting, stream flushing, and kernel-crossing overhead for the same records.

metrics.label: Instructions
metrics.explanation: Retired instructions show how much stream-management work each strategy performs.

metrics.label: IPC
metrics.explanation: IPC helps separate front-end execution from time lost across frequent stream flushes.

metrics.label: Branches
metrics.explanation: The buffer adds checks but avoids repeating the deeper flush path for every record.

metrics.label: Branch-miss rate
metrics.explanation: This rate provides context; total cycles and calls to the output path are the primary evidence.

metrics.label: Cache misses
metrics.explanation: Cache misses are a control metric because buffering mainly targets I/O boundary overhead.

learning.change: Replace a flush after every record with bounded user-space buffers and bulk writes.
learning.hypothesis: If fixed output-boundary costs dominate, batching the same bytes should reduce cycles and runtime without changing file contents.
learning.caution: The reference counters come from one Linux processor. Local runtime varies with the stream implementation and operating system.
prompts: Which calling-context path becomes cheaper when thousands of std::endl flushes become a few bulk writes?
Do the instruction and cycle changes support a syscall-bound explanation, or a cache-locality explanation?
When would buffering provide little benefit or increase latency?
